policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads 'Christ, who is our life' (ἡμῶν) and relegates the base ὑμῶν to the mapped textual note 'Many ancient authorities read your.'
ASV 'your members' does not distinguish an expressed ὑμῶν from the article τὰ alone: English idiom supplies the possessive for a body-part noun either way, and no note touches it.
ASV prints 'upon the sons of disobedience' in the text and the mapped textual note reports the omission as 'Some ancient authorities omit'.
ASV 'when ye lived in these things' renders the demonstrative τούτοις, not the pronoun αὐτοῖς ('in them'). The 'Or, amongst whom' note is an alternative_rendering of ἐν οἷς and decides nothing here.
The article τὰ before πάντα has no separate exponent in ASV 'Christ is all, and in all'; presence or absence renders identically.
ASV text reads 'even as the Lord forgave you' (κύριος) and the mapped textual note carries Χριστός as 'Many ancient authorities read Christ.'
ASV 'which is the bond of perfectness' renders ὅ and ἥτις alike; English 'which' does not distinguish the relative from the indefinite relative.
ASV 'the peace of Christ' names Χριστοῦ, not θεοῦ; the only note here is a greek_gloss on 'rule'.
ASV 'psalms and hymns and spiritual songs' does not settle καί: an English list of three requires conjunctions whether the Greek is asyndetic or joined.
Same as the preceding conjunction in the list: ASV's 'and' between 'hymns' and 'spiritual songs' is required English regardless of whether καί stands after ὕμνοις.
ASV 'singing with grace' renders ἐν χάριτι with or without the article; ASV routinely leaves an article before an abstract noun unrendered.
ASV 'in your hearts' is plural, rendering ταῖς καρδίαις rather than the singular τῇ καρδίᾳ.
ASV 'unto God' renders θεῷ, not κυρίῳ. The 'the Lord; others God' note belongs to 'the word of Christ' at the head of the verse, not to this dative.
ὅ τι and ὅτι differ only in word division; ASV 'whatsoever ye do' renders either.
ἐάν and ἄν are interchangeable in the indefinite relative clause; ASV 'whatsoever' shows no difference.
ASV 'giving thanks to God the Father' has no conjunction; the added καί would give 'God and the Father'.
ASV 'be in subjection to your husbands' lacks 'own'; ASV renders ἴδιος in this formula as 'own' (Eph. 5:22), so its absence points to the article alone.
The variant is only the order of εὐάρεστόν and ἐστιν; ASV 'this is well-pleasing' fixes English order independently of it.
ASV 'not with eye-service' is a mass noun that renders the plural ὀφθαλμοδουλίαις and the singular alike; the notes here are greek_glosses on 'Servants' and 'masters'.
ASV 'fearing the Lord' renders τὸν κύριον, not τὸν θεόν.
ASV begins 'whatsoever ye do' with no connective and no 'all'; the RP reading καὶ πᾶν ὅ τι would yield 'And whatsoever'.
ἀπολήμψεσθε and λήψεσθε are both 'ye shall receive' in ASV; the compound is not separately exponed, 'recompense' rendering ἀνταπόδοσιν.
ASV 'ye serve the Lord Christ' follows the colon with no 'for'; the added γάρ would be rendered.
ASV opens the verse 'For he that doeth wrong', rendering γάρ rather than δέ.
